_note: Narrative contribution to docs/briefs/BOUNDARIES.md (layer 2: diegetic blockers). The engine owns placement, colliders and region bounds. 'edge' and 'at' are PROVISIONAL until the expanded bounds are confirmed (requested: west about Ninth/Tenth Ave, north about 47th St). All names are invented; real public institutions (the police) appear by office only. Bark lines are 90 characters or fewer and work as subtitles.

film.title: NIGHT RATE
film.logline_on_call_sheet: A night-shift cabbie, a missing fare, and a city that won't stop the meter.
film.director: Lew Abernathy (invented; never seen, always 'Mr. Abernathy wants quiet')
film.first_ad: Bobbi Sarno (invented; the voice on the bullhorn)
film.slate: NIGHT RATE · PROD. 7406 · SC. 41 · TK. 9 · DIR. ABERNATHY · CAM. B
signs: FILMING IN PROGRESS — PLEASE USE OTHER STREET
QUIET PLEASE — ROLLING WHEN RED LIGHT IS ON
film.why: Location crime pictures were common on 1974 NYC streets, and the shoot echoes the game's own 35mm look. At night it's the best-lit block in the city.

agencies.name: Hudson Union Steam & Power

fiction.workSuspendedSign: WORK SUSPENDED — FUNDS PENDING — BUREAU OF STREET OPENINGS
fiction._workSuspendedWhy: The fiscal-crisis nod: by late summer, trenches stay open because the city can't pay to close them. These signs multiply as the acts go on (P5).

blockers.note: Wraps the day Act 3 begins. The PAs' last bark on 7 Aug is the wrap call. In daytime the trucks are parked but there's no shoot (the trucks still block the street).

blockers.sign: WORK SUSPENDED — FUNDS PENDING — BUREAU OF STREET OPENINGS
blockers.note: Replaces the film shoot in the same spot. A city with no money leaves the hole open.
Real: the Penn Central rail yards in a sunken cut. A chain-link fence, rusted signal masts, freight cars. No barks; ambient yard sounds come from the audio team.
Real: the tunnel-approach trench. The traffic jam into it is the edge (layer 3).
Real: the elevated West Side Highway, closed after its December 1973 collapse. It's visible from the western streets, rusting and empty.
Wooden police sawhorses and a beat cop waving people off. In chases this is the roadblock. On the night of 8 Aug (M22) a crowd collects here around a radio in a parked cab.
Striped steam chimney venting; steel plates; at night a lit flasher on a sawhorse. In Act 3 the work-suspended sign goes up.
The heat-wave water-main break: a flooded block, a geyser, the Board's truck. Content rule: children appear only playing at an opened hydrant on a different, safe corner, never in traffic or danger.
A block association's summer party: card tables, a bandstand of folding chairs, a salsa trio, kids' races at the far end. It's passable on foot, and the crowd thickens into layer 3.
The second unit of NIGHT RATE shooting a cab chase. Gives the south edge a reason on weeknights in Act 2.

brownoutVariant._note: On brownout nights (ENGINE_REQUESTS #2) blockers stay physical but lose their lights. The film shoot runs on its own generators and becomes the only bright block for miles, which is a useful landmark on dark nights. Barricades get kerosene flare pots. Utility crews work by truck headlight.

actChanges.summary: Every blocker is fresh and busy. NIGHT RATE shoots at night on the west edge; trenches are staffed; weekend block parties start.
Heat and money run out. The east water main breaks; NIGHT RATE adds a second unit on the south edge; trenches are half-staffed, and the first work-suspended signs appear.

NIGHT RATE wraps (flag.act3_started), and its west-edge street becomes an abandoned trench, a hole the city can't afford to fill. Work-suspended signs are everywhere. On 8 Aug a crowd gathers at the north barricade around a cab radio.
October: the trenches are still open. If the engine later expands the region, a blocker is simply removed to open the next district (for example the west trench is finally filled).

barks.film_pa.text: Picture's up! Hold it right there, pal!
Rolling! Nobody moves! That means you in the hat!
Sir, this is a closed set. Use Forty-Third.
Mr. Abernathy wants quiet. I want a sandwich. Nobody's happy.
You want to be in pictures? Stand right there and look tired. Perfect.
Background, cross! Cab, wait for my hand! And… hold.
Hey! You walked through take nine! Do you know what film costs?
Reset! Back to one! Somebody wet the street again!
Coffee's for crew. You look like crew. Don't tell anybody.
Car coming through! Is that ours? That's not ours! Stop that car!
No, we're not the TV news. We're the movie about the TV news' bad night.
Street's closed till four a.m. Union rules. Take it up with the union.
Lock it up! Lock it up! Picture's up on the corner!
Autographs after wrap. Not mine. I'm nobody.
This block's playing Cleveland tonight. Go around, it's cheaper.
Wet down the street again. Mr. Abernathy says the dry looks fake.
Kill the radio! Whose radio? Kill it!
That's a wrap on Forty-Fourth, folks! Thanks for nothing, New York!

barks.barricade_cop.text: Street's closed. Go around.
Nothing to see. Keep it moving.
Around the block, buddy. Same as everybody.
You deaf? I said closed. C-L-O-S-E-D.
Twelve hours on a sawhorse. Don't make it thirteen.
Use the avenue. That's what it's there for.
Back it up. Back it UP. There you go.
What's going on? Overtime is what's going on.
Sidewalk only, ma'am. Watch the plates.
Hey, hey, hey! Not past the horses!
City pays me to stand here. Barely. So I'm standing.
Detour's posted. Read the sign.
If I knew why it's closed, I'd be a sergeant.
You honk one more time, you're getting a ticket for music.
Turn it around, pal. Nice and easy.
Hot enough for you? Me neither. Go around.
Nobody in, nobody out. Orders.
Best seat in the city and I can't sit down.
Lady, I don't care if you live there. Use the other end.
Move along. The night's long enough.
Whoa! Whoa! Slow down! This is a roadblock!
Pull over! Pull it over right now!
Get him at the horses! He's not getting through here!
You'd have had better luck through the Lincoln Tunnel, wise guy.
Rain. Of course it's rain. Go around, folks.
Watch the puddle. It's deeper than it looks.
Lights out on the whole block and they still want me standing here.
Mind the flare pots. Go around.
You hear the radio? He's going. Tomorrow noon, they're saying.
History's on the radio, pal. Traffic's still on the avenue.
Running? Nobody runs past me. Walk it.
Easy with the shoving. I got nowhere to put you either.

barks.utility_crew.text: Steam main. Don't stand on the plates.
Hole's been here since June. It'll be here at Christmas.
Funds pending. Means we wait. Means you go around.
Hudson Union, buddy. We own under the street. You own the sidewalk.
Back up! She's venting! Back up!
City says fix it. City says no money. We dig half a hole.
Main's busted. Whole block's a swimming pool. Go around.
Hundred and four in the trench today. Bring me a soda or go away.
Lights are out? Not my department. Ask the other guys in our department.
Plates are hot. Shoes'll melt. Your call.
Work suspended. That's not a sign, that's a philosophy.
Truck's coming out backwards. Clear the way.

barks.block_party.text: Block party! Cars go around, people come in!
Two raffle tickets for a quarter. Prize is a fan. A fan, in July!
You live on this block? You do now. Grab a plate.
Band's on at eight. They know three songs. Very well.
Mister, that's the dance floor. Walk around the dance floor.
Block association thanks you. Dues are two dollars. Kidding. Mostly.
Who made the pernil? Whoever made the pernil, marry me.
Street's closed for the party. Park on the avenue, come back hungry.
Cops gave us till eleven. Cops always give us till eleven.
Rain? Rain's just free air-conditioning. Keep playing!
Easy, you'll knock the cake over. The cake is the whole party.
Lights out? Bring the candles! Party's not over!

barks.brownout_edge.text: Whole city's dark and the movie people still got lights. Figures.
Careful, no streetlights past here. Go around by the avenue.
Hudson Union says an hour. Hudson Union always says an hour.
Watch it! Signal's out! Nobody's got the light!
